prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” agent for every seller — the right agent depends on your neighborhood, price range, timeline and priorities (highest price vs fastest sale, marketing style, fees, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. Below is a practical approach plus an offer to pull a short, evidence-based shortlist if you want.

How to find the best agent for your Pleasanton home
1. Decide your priorities
   - Maximize sale price? Fast sale? Low commission? Specialized buyers (luxury, move-up, downsizing)?
2. Look for evidence of performance
   - Recent comparable listings sold in Pleasanton (same neighborhood, similar beds/baths and price)
   - List price vs sold price, and average days on market
   - Number of closings per year (experience)
3. Where to search and check
   - Realtor.com, Zillow, Redfin agent pages (recent sales, reviews)
   - Local MLS data (through agents) or county records for verified sales
   - Google and Yelp reviews, Nextdoor and local Facebook groups for homeowner recommendations
   - Brokerages active in Pleasanton (Compass, Keller Williams, Coldwell Banker, Intero, Lyon, etc.) — teams often handle complex marketing
4. What to ask when you interview agents
   - What recent, comparable Pleasanton homes have you sold? Can you provide a CMA?
   - What was the list-to-sale price and days on market for those?
   - What’s your marketing plan (professional photos, staging, online ads, open houses, broker tours, targeted outreach)?
   - How do you communicate and how often?
   - Who on your team will handle escrow, showings and paperwork?
   - What are your fees and any additional costs?
   - Can you provide references from recent Pleasanton sellers?
5. Red flags to avoid
   - Vague answers about comparable sales or marketing plan
   - Pressure to accept a low listing price or sign an exclusive contract without a plan
   - Poor or no references, inconsistent communication
6. Typical commission and terms in your area
   - In the Bay Area, total commission commonly runs around 5–6% (split between listing and buyer agents), but this can vary. Some agents offer alternative fee structures — weigh cost vs services.

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short, evidence-based shortlist (3–5 agents or teams) who’ve recently sold homes similar to yours in Pleasanton, showing their recent sold prices, days on market and links to reviews. I’ll need the property address (or ZIP), approximate home type (beds/baths, size) and your priorities/timeline.

Tell me the address or the ZIP and what’s most important to you, and I’ll prepare a tailored short list and recommended questions to ask each agent.
